play_summary: You climbed the mountain in the game. You move between lanes on the rock wall and climb up to the summit at 120 m. Your stamina goes down over time; you refill it with water bottles found on the wall. The weather changes with the altitude: clear skies at the bottom, wind from 30 m (gusts push you to another lane), rain from 60 m (you climb slower, you get tired faster and the rock has slippery or icy patches), and a storm from 90 m (lightning strikes, strong gusts, more falling rocks). Falling rocks come down during the whole climb. When you fall, you start again at the beginning of the current weather section.

questions.text: How difficult was the climb for you, from 1 (very easy) to 7 (very hard)? Why?
The weather got worse as you climbed: rain, gusts, lightning, falling rocks and icy patches. Did that make you think about climate change? Why or why not?
You said that the weather on a mountain has always been wild. Did this climb change that idea, even a little?
Did any moment of the climb feel unfair or preachy?
Would you play it again? What would you change?
Which answer of the player convinced you the most, and which one annoyed you?
Did the facts from the IPCC report feel trustworthy in the conversation? Why?

statements_note: Our own statements, one per dimension of the CCS-Q (Climate Change Skepticism Questionnaire). They are NOT the official questionnaire items.

statements.text: The climate is not really warming faster than in the past.
Recent warming is mostly caused by natural factors, not by humans.
The consequences of climate change are exaggerated.
What I do personally makes no difference for the climate.
